newsitem.title: UK: NWE oil products firmer across the barrel.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products firmer across the barrel.

text.p: NWE oil products were firmer across the barrel on Monday morning as talk of further sanctions by the United Nations against Iraq lifted crude and products futures, traders said.

Gasoline prices were firmer in line with crude and NYMEX gasoline futures. Traders said the Eurograde market continued to talk on a two-tier basis with Rotterdam refinery barges assessed around $4 a tonne over those with general ARA options.
Naphtha prices were firmer on the back of crude, but traders said spot price gains were mostly notional with relaxed buying keeping bids low while term contract pricing kept offers high.
Gas oil was dragged higher by benchmark IPE gas oil futures. Heating oil barge premiums were little changed at July IPE -50 cents/flat fob ARA for end-June and first half July delivery.

High sulphur barges were steady to a shade firmer on relatively better demand, done at $82.50 to $83 a tonne fob ARA after earlier trades at $82 and initially at $82.75. Low sulphur barges were talked unchanged at $94/$96.
High sulphur cargoes were quietly offered and several Russian E-4 cargoes were also on offer at premiums of $3.5-$5 to three means.
